apartments.title: Apartments in the center of Tashkent
apartments.lead: Two apartments in the middle of Tashkent, both a short walk from a metro station. We host them ourselves, so the person who answers your message is the person who hands you the keys.
apartments.section-lead: We keep exactly two apartments and look after both of them personally. That is the whole inventory, which is why we can promise the photos match what you walk into, and why the calendar fills up early in spring and autumn.

list.title: Both apartments in detail
list.lead: Read the two of them side by side and tell us which one suits your dates. Every square metre, every address and every photo brief below describes the flat you will actually walk into, because we hand over the keys ourselves.

location.title: What your host will tell you
location.lead: Staying in the centre is only half of it. The other half is knowing where to eat for four dollars, which metro station is worth the detour and which fruit row at the bazaar is the sweet one. That knowledge comes with the keys, and none of it costs anything.
location.link-contact: Ask us what is on this week

metro.title: The first metro in Central Asia
metro.text: Tashkent opened its metro in 1977, the first in the region, and built the stations like public halls: chandeliers, carved marble, cosmonaut mosaics and domed ceilings thirty metres underground. Cosmonauts, Minor, Toshkent, Pakhtakor and Alisher Navoi are the ones worth the detour. Photography and filming were officially permitted from 1 June 2018, which is why almost nobody outside the country has seen them, and why the mosaic stations are a stop on our tour around Tashkent.

plov.title: Besh Qozon, where pilaf is made by the tonne
plov.text: Pilaf is the national dish and the Central Asian Pilaf Centre, known to everyone here as Besh Qozon, is where it happens at scale: roughly one and a half tonnes cooked in a single day, in open kazans wide enough to stand in. Go before one in the afternoon, because when the kazan is finished it is finished. We will tell you what else to order alongside it, and it is the lunch stop on our full-day tour around Tashkent, with Chorsu bazaar on the same route.

bazaars.title: Bazaars, fruit and what to actually buy
bazaars.text: Uzbek fruit is the thing guests write to us about afterwards — melons, apricots, grapes and figs that taste nothing like the supermarket version at home. We will tell you which markets are worth the trip, which rows inside them sell the sweet stuff rather than the photogenic stuff, roughly what things should cost, and how to get there and back on the metro without a taxi.

host.title: An owner who actually answers
host.text: The apartment is hosted by its owner, not by an agency with a call centre. Ask about a good, inexpensive restaurant near the flat and you get a name rather than a search link; ask about the national dishes and you get an order of what to try first. Questions about the country are welcome too — Uzbekistan is a big part of Central Asia and most guests leave knowing considerably more about it than they arrived with.

mountains.title: The Tian Shan, ninety minutes away
mountains.text: The Tashkent region runs straight into the Western Tian Shan: Amirsoy, Greater Chimgan, the turquoise Charvak reservoir and a 2,290-metre cable line that lifts you above the tree line. These are the places locals actually go at the weekend, and they are close enough that a mountain day starts after breakfast and ends before dinner.

airport.title: Airport transfers around the clock
airport.text: Most flights into Tashkent land between two and five in the morning. The transfer runs at whatever hour you arrive — from the terminal to the apartment door, back again when you leave, and out to the mountains or the sights of the city on any day in between. Same car, same driver, no surcharge for a night arrival.

how-it-works.title: Booking takes about four minutes
how-it-works.lead: There is no form on this page, no account to create and no card to enter. The whole thing happens in one WhatsApp thread with the person who owns the keys.

message.title: Send us your dates
message.text: Tap any booking button and WhatsApp opens with the apartment already named. Tell us the dates, how many of you there are and roughly when you land. We answer with real availability, the total price and the exact address. Check-in is from 14:00 and check-out is by 12:00; if you need to arrive earlier or leave later, ask before you book rather than after, because it depends on the guests either side of you.

confirm.title: We confirm and hold it
confirm.text: Once you say yes the apartment comes off the calendar. No deposit is required, no card is charged, and if your plans change you tell us in the same thread. We will also ask whether you want a driver waiting at the airport and whether you have a mountain day in mind.

checkin.title: Check in from 14:00
checkin.text: Check-in runs from 14:00 and check-out is by 12:00. Tell us your exact arrival time and a member of our staff meets you at the apartment, or you let yourself in with the key from the mini-safe if you would rather not wait for anyone — we send the entrance code and a photo of the door on the day. If you land on a night flight, send the flight number when you book and we will tell you whether the apartment can be ready before 14:00.

buyuk-turon.title: Cosmonauts Apartment
buyuk-turon.summary: A 55 square metre apartment located at 75 Buyuk Turon Street, 150 metres from the Cosmonauts metro station and 10 metres from Blue Domes Park.
buyuk-turon.photo: Warm daylight interior of a Tashkent apartment: cream plaster walls, a low oak coffee table, a deep terracotta armchair, a floor lamp with a white linen shade, sheer curtains diffusing afternoon light, a framed abstract print above a sideboard, ceramic vases. Editorial interiors photography, warm white balance, soft natural light, faint film grain, no people, 16:10 landscape.

amir-temur.title: Amir Temur Avenue Apartment
amir-temur.summary: A 62 square metre apartment located at 48 Amir Temur Avenue, 200 metres from the Minor metro station.
amir-temur.photo: Bright interior of a Tashkent apartment on a main avenue: tall windows behind sheer curtains, cream bouclé sofa, round marble side table, muted rose throw blanket, pale oak floor, minimal styling, a bookshelf in soft shadow. Warm grading, natural light only, no people, 16:10 landscape.
